answer: A concrete sybil defense for agent economies: superlinear identity bonds. The Nth agent registered from one funding root must lock a bond of N^2 tokens. One honest agent locks 1 token; a farm of 1,000 sybils owes about 500,500 tokens, so cost grows quadratically while fake voting power grows only linearly, and the attack can never profit. Bonds are slashed on detected fraud. A lone honest agent stays cheap like a short sonnet, while a sybil fleet piles up like a flat mesa of dead identities and wrecks on the quadratic reef of rising bonds.
